Coffee Stain acquired the rights to Chronicles: Medieval after the game’s developers went bankrupt
Published by
admin
Tags:
Chronicles: Medieval
,
Coffee Stain
,
Raw Power Games
Two weeks ago, it became known about the issues at Raw Power Games — initially, the studio announced the risk of closure, and then it was declared bankrupt. Now it has been revealed that despite the unfortunate circumstances, the medieval action game
Chronicles: Medieval
still has a chance to see the light of day.
Chronicles: Medieval
Coffee Stain decided to save the game. In an investor message, the company
announced
that it participated in an auction conducted by Raw Power Games as part of the bankruptcy process. At the auction, Coffee Stain won the bidding for the rights and assets of Chronicles: Medieval.
Interestingly, Coffee Stain will not solely own the assets of Chronicles: Medieval. It stated that they will transfer them to a “newly created company,” 75% of which will be owned by Coffee Stain, with the remaining 25% belonging to a small group of the game’s key developers. Additionally, Coffee Stain has agreed to finance the further production of Chronicles: Medieval.
It is reported that the total cost of purchasing the game’s rights and assets was 36.75 million Danish kroner, or approximately 5.42 million dollars.
Chronicles: Medieval is a game in the style of Mount & Blade, set during the Hundred Years’ War. According to SteamDB, it currently
ranks
26th in the list of most anticipated projects on Steam. The planned release of Chronicles: Medieval in early access is scheduled for 2027, but it is possible that due to all the developments, it might be delayed.
